heading: Explore a change. See what the numbers mean.
description: Every lesson is one frozen source, one policy, and one result produced by diffdevil.

entries.title: The lockfile is still part of the change
entries.summary: An explicit exclusion changes the question, not the observed source.
guide: This Vite dependency update changes a manifest and its lockfile. Start with both files: a policy has not made the lockfile disappear from the observed comparison.
Raw churn counts a removed version and its replacement separately. Replacement-aware lines pair that local edit while keeping unrelated lockfile additions visible.
Switch to Exclude the lockfile, then back again. The policy answers a narrower question; it does not claim the whole pull request became smaller.

entries.title: A small helper can touch a wide surface
entries.summary: Replacement-aware counting and file spread are different facts.
guide: This runtime change replaces repeated null guards with a common API across implementation and nested tests.
The line result is asymmetric: a compact replacement can remove more source than it adds. File count remains its own fact, not a proxy for risk or effort.
The implementation scope intentionally excludes nested tests. The whole-change result keeps them, so the two views can be compared without erasing either.

entries.title: Snapshots are material, not invisible background
entries.summary: Overlapping scopes describe the same change from different angles.
guide: A formatting change can carry implementation, documentation, tests, and generated snapshots in one comparison.
The scopes overlap on purpose. They are not percentages to add together; each is a named view of the same retained source evidence.
Select the scope variant to inspect those views. diffdevil reports the actual selected policy rather than calling the change formatting-only.

entries.title: Binary files still count as evidence
entries.summary: Unmeasurable line facts are neither zero nor an omission.
guide: This change contains Rust, workflow and lockfile edits alongside six committed executable trampoline files.
The six binary records remain in the whole comparison, with unmeasurable line values. A blank number is a fact about the material, not permission to substitute zero.
The text-only variant excludes exactly those paths. It is useful for a text question, but it is honestly labelled as a narrower selection.

entries.title: Same line total, different file spread
entries.summary: Equal totals do not erase file distribution.
guide: Both authored inputs add twenty-four lines. One puts twelve lines in each of two files; the other spreads two lines across twelve files.
The aggregate changed-line measurement is deliberately equal. The file records make the distribution visible without turning it into a claim about complexity or quality.
Move between the two variants. The source identity follows the selected patch, so an export never implies that the other shape produced the result.

entries.title: A bounded value can still prove a policy
entries.summary: A rule can hold when evidence cannot establish its condition.
guide: This saved report preserves a changed-line interval instead of an invented exact total.
Under the first policy every possible value lies below one hundred, so that band is proven. Under the second policy the interval crosses sixty-five, so the label group holds.
Queries show the same distinction: above fifty is true, above seventy is false, and above sixty-five remains unknown.

entries.title: Observed files are not the whole inventory
entries.summary: A partial file list does not license invented paths.
guide: The report knows there are three files but contains only one observed record.
The visible row remains useful evidence. Overall line counts keep their lower bound and unknown standing because the missing members cannot be named or measured.
A rendering limit and an incomplete source inventory are different facts. This example preserves the latter rather than filling the list with guesses.
